topics.label: Lecture framing: cancer hallmarks and loss of growth control
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s aims and the hallmark framework used to interpret cancer-associated mutations.

topics.label: Mutations that deregulate extracellular growth signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways free cancer cells from normal controls on proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in blood and intestinal cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how disrupted cell maturation contributes to cancer and becomes visible in the affected tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered p53 signaling and the balance of mitochondrial apoptotic regulators allow cancer cells to avoid death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how increased telomerase expression enables cancer cells to bypass it.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consolidate how cellular safeguards constrain damaged cells and how mutation-driven cancer hallmarks overcome normal growth control.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine altered cancer metabolism as a functional hallmark that can both reflect and reinforce tumor development.

topics.label: Angiogenesis as vascular support for tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors recruit blood vessels to sustain growth beyond the limits of oxygen and nutrient diffusion.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and survival at secondary sites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells spread and establish secondary tumors despite the biological barriers to successful metastasis.

topics.label: Closing summary and further reading on cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This closing restates the lecture’s central takeaway and directs students toward further reading and the upcoming practicals.
